stop_condition: Every claim introduced by the three substantive working-tree edits (A: README floor row + new paragraph; B: workflow-doctor.sh validated-set 1.1.2:53 entry; C: workflow-doctor.sh NEARLY-read-only comment) is shown TRUE and SYMMETRIC -- neither overstating the doubt nor presenting an inference as an observation (rubric C9); claim (C)'s side effect AND its stated precondition are re-derived independently rather than inherited; (B) is checked against the surrounding definition, the EXACT MEMBERSHIP paragraph and the UPDATE PROCEDURE in its own file; every surface that could assert 'CI validates the bd 1.1.2 floor' or 'the doctor run is read-only' is swept with a positive control on each search; the three cheap checks pass at the stated counts; and the working tree is shown uncontaminated before and after.

findings.evidence: RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY, not inherited. Host: bd 1.3.0 (f45b249ce), dolt 2.3.0 -- the same dolt release the comment names. Instrument: `find <store> -mindepth 1 | sort` before/after, with a POSITIVE CONTROL run FIRST (touched <store>/.qa-control-probe; the diff printed exactly that one path; probe removed and the pre-snapshot retaken). All fixtures built under the session scratchpad with an isolated HOME and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL; nothing written into the repo. ARM A -- POPULATED store (`git init` + `bd init --database beads --non-interactive` + 3 `bd create`; `.dolt/stats` confirmed ABSENT first): running EXACTLY workflow-doctor.sh:1501-1502, `( cd <store> && dolt sql -r csv -q "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version),0) FROM schema_migrations" )`, returned 66 and took the store from 11 to 22 paths. The 11 new paths are .dolt/stats, .dolt/stats/.dolt, and beneath it config.json, noms/LOCK, noms/journal.idx, noms/manifest, noms/oldgen, noms/vvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvv, repo_state.json, temptf. A second, independently built populated store (5 issues) gave 11 again. So the comment's COUNT (11) and SHAPE ('a nested .dolt with its own noms/, manifest and LOCK') are exactly right, and so is its dolt version. ARM B -- stats already present (same store, SELECT re-run): 0 new, 0 removed. The comment's second negative arm is RIGHT. ARM C -- EMPTY store: `bd init --database beads --non-interactive` with NO issues created (`bd list --json` -> 0 ids), `.dolt/stats` absent: the SAME SELECT returned 66 and created THE SAME 11 PATHS, 10 -> 21. Repeated on a second empty store: 11 again. n=2 on each arm, all three arms reproducible.
findings.description: The clause 'It creates nothing on an empty store' is FALSE, measured twice. The side effect fires on an empty bd store exactly as it does on a populated one, so the precondition this comment introduces is NARROWER THAN THE EFFECT IT DESCRIBES -- the unsafe direction. On my measurements the only condition that matters is that `.dolt/stats/` does not already exist; whether the store holds issues is irrelevant. The attribution that follows is affected too: 'which is why the first two attempts to reproduce it came back clean' names emptiness as a cause that arm C rules out. A likelier explanation for at least one clean attempt is on this host -- this repo's OWN store already has stats (`ls -d .beads/embeddeddolt/beads/.dolt/stats` -> present), which is also why a full suite run here leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. This matters precisely because of the lesson the edit itself records: a side-effect claim needs its precondition stated with it. The replacement precondition is wrong, and it is a NEW false claim introduced by this diff rather than a pre-existing one -- a reader is told an empty store is safe when it is not. Everything else in edit C that I could reach reproduced exactly.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh:149-153 (unmodified) against 154-170 (edit B); same conflict at 174-178, 233-238 and 1545-1547
findings.evidence: Line 149-153, unchanged by this diff, reads: 'ONLY TWO OF THE FOUR MEASURED PAIRS ARE VALIDATED BELOW, DELIBERATELY. "Validated" means a suite this project actually runs exercises the pair, not merely that it was measured once above -- claiming an unexercised pair as validated would be the exact defect family this pin exists to catch, committed by the pin's own constant:'. The first of the two members it then introduces is the one edit B rewrites to say, at 159-161, 'by this header's own definition of "validated" ... the entry is currently unsupported'. Three further unmodified passages state the admission rule the retained entry now breaks: 174-178 ('1.2.1:65 and 1.2.2:53 are measured above but exercised by no suite, so they are KNOWN, not validated, and are deliberately left out of the set ... do not add a pair on the strength of a one-off measurement alone, here or anywhere this pattern recurs'); the UPDATE PROCEDURE at 233-238 ('then, ONLY once a suite exercises the new pair ... add ... Until it has coverage, record it in this header as measured-but-unvalidated instead of adding it to the set'); and the OPERATOR-FACING fix text printed on a DRIFT FAIL at 1545-1547, which restates it verbatim. Edit B's own justification at 168-170 is 'The entry STAYS because the pair is correct' -- i.e. on the strength of a measurement, which is what 177-178 forbids. The EXACT MEMBERSHIP paragraph (180-188) is NOT in conflict: it is about membership-vs-floor and the visible pass, and the new text is compatible with it.
findings.description: Direct answer to the brief's question 3: yes, edit B fights the surrounding definition. The header's count sentence is the file's own summary of the list it introduces, and after this edit it asserts that two pairs meet a definition the file then says one of them does not meet -- so the sentence is false by the file's own terms, five lines above the entry that falsifies it. The same sentence warns that doing this is 'the exact defect family this pin exists to catch, committed by the pin's own constant', which is now a description of the file's own state. Separately, the set retains a member the file's stated admission rule says must be recorded as measured-but-unvalidated and left out; the new text gives a reason for keeping it (removing a true pair would make it read as drift -- sound on its own) but does not reconcile that reason with the three places stating the opposite rule, one of which is text an operator READS at the moment the check fails. The correction landed on the member entry and stopped there.

findings.location: .claude/commands/workflow-doctor.md:56-58 (MANIFESTED) plus .claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh:61-63, :388-390 (--help) and :1354-1356 -- none touched by edit C
findings.evidence: Edit C corrects ONE sentence. The same proposition stands, unmodified, in four other places, found by `grep -niE 'only file change|modifies nothing|read[- ]only|touches nothing|never writes|side.effect' .claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh` (positive control on the same file: `grep -nicE 'DOCTOR_BD_SCHEMA_VALIDATED'` -> 16, so the search works): (1) file header :61-63 -- 'On an isolated 6,936-file target: a full run changed exactly those three .beads/* files and nothing else'; (2) the --help body :388-390, which an operator reads -- 'Measured on a 6,936-file target: a full run changed exactly those three and nothing else'; (3) the beads check's OWN header :1354-1356, 75 lines above the edit -- 'This is the only file change a full run makes anywhere in the target (QA verified against an isolated 10,358-file tree)', and the new comment at :1447 sends the reader TO that header ('see this check's header') for the side-effect story; (4) the skill `.claude/commands/workflow-doctor.md`:56-58 -- 'Measured on a 6,936-file target: those three files are the ONLY things a full run modifies anywhere, and a run with `--skip beads` modifies nothing at all.' The skill is a SHIPPED artifact: `grep -n 'commands/workflow-doctor.md' manifests/v5.0.0.sha256` -> row 12. Edit C's own new sentence at :1441-1442 says 'the skill's "a run with --skip beads modifies nothing at all" is about the SKIPPED case and is unaffected'. That is true of the clause it quotes, and the quoted clause is the only part of that sentence which IS unaffected -- the clause immediately before it, in the same sentence, is the one R2-F1's measurement falsifies. Checked and NOT affected: the enumerated list at :376-380 (settings.json, SKILL.md, issues.jsonl, model: pins ...) stays true, `.dolt/stats` being none of those; and docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:822's 'only a run with --skip beads provably touches nothing' also stays true, since --skip beads skips the SELECT too.
findings.description: Direct answer to the brief's question 4 for the read-only proposition: NO, it is not fixed everywhere. One sentence is corrected and four restatements of the same thing are left standing, three of them in the very file being edited -- including the user-facing --help text and the same function's own header, which the new comment then cites as authority. The fourth is in a manifested, shipped skill. The claims are general ('the ONLY things a full run modifies anywhere', 'the only file change a full run makes anywhere in the target'), and the case that falsifies them is the common one, not an exotic one: a store whose `.dolt/stats` does not yet exist, which is every freshly initialised bd store (measured -- neither `bd init` nor `bd create` creates stats). The sentence declaring the skill 'unaffected' is the sharpest part: it is a positive non-impact claim about another shipped file, made without the adjacent clause being checked, and a reader who trusts it will not go and look. This is the claude-workflow-plugin-38cd shape -- a correction scoped to a sentence rather than to a proposition.

findings.location: .github/workflows/test.yml:218-231 -- not in the diff, not manifested, but a repo surface asserting the withdrawn proposition
findings.evidence: The CORRECTION paragraph at :218-231 reads, present tense: 'DOCTOR_BD_SCHEMA_PIN (a single exact pair) became DOCTOR_BD_SCHEMA_VALIDATED (a membership set), specifically including `1.1.2:53` -- THIS job's own pinned pair -- alongside `1.3.0:66`. META-TEST 8's control now PASSES here, because this job's live pair is a validated member, not because the check stopped checking.' Both halves are now contradicted, and I measured the contradiction rather than inferring it. `gh run view 36971074875 --json headSha,jobs` -> headSha=ed9ea91e6496ce13a5c080ad3cbbb2dc14ba7e66 (exactly this working tree's HEAD), run conclusion=failure, job 'L1 -- bash unit tests' conclusion=FAILURE. In that job's log: 'FAIL: META-TEST 8a control: beads PASSES against a freshly bd-init'd "beads"-named fixture' and 'FAIL: META-TEST 8a control: ...and the note names the validated set, not just "OK"'. The observed pair, from the doctor's own new disclosure: '[8a] measured: bd-version-vs-schema DRIFT: installed bd 1.3.1 / store schema v66 is not in the validated set {1.1.2:53 1.3.0:66}'. So (a) the control does NOT pass there, and (b) the job's live pair is not 1.1.2:53. Positive control on the log search: the same file matched 'Install bd' 33 times and '1.1.2' 6 times, so an empty result would have been meaningful; gh prefixes every line with job/step/timestamp, so nothing was anchored to start-of-line. By contrast :208-211 of the same paragraph ('Measured directly ... against THIS job's exact pinned pair (bd 1.1.2 + dolt 2.3.5): the live pair is `1.1.2:53`') describes a container reproduction of the PINS, not the job, and remains the same true statement edit A and edit B both keep.
findings.description: Answer to the brief's question 4 for the floor proposition. README, CHANGELOG, docs/, the skill and the agent prompts are CLEAN -- I swept them (`grep -rnE 'floor'` over README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md, docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, .github/workflows/test.yml, .claude/commands/*.md, .claude/agents/*.md, with a positive control; and every 1.1.2 mention in each doc surface read individually). CHANGELOG:2151 ('installs the real bd, pinned v1.1.2'), :2256 ('the version CI pins') and :2758-2760 ('a new CI job l1-doctor-bd-max pins the upper end') all say INSTALLS or PINS, never validates or measures, so they survive. The one surface left asserting it is this CI-config comment, and it asserts it in a stronger form than the README row ever did -- it names the job's live pair as 1.1.2:53 and gives that as the REASON the control passes. It also now carries a plainly checkable present-tense falsehood ('now PASSES here') at this exact HEAD. It is not a manifested artifact (`grep -c 'workflows/test.yml' manifests/v5.0.0.sha256` -> 0), so whether it blocks the tag is the operator's call; what it is NOT is clean.

findings.evidence: The table's other three rows use one vocabulary: 'validated -- ...' (in the set) and 'measured, not validated -- no suite exercises it' (out of the set), so status doubles as set membership. The new row uses a third form, 'pair measured directly; CI floor coverage UNCONFIRMED -- see below', which states neither membership nor non-membership; the new paragraph at 384-395 does not state it either. A reader running bd 1.1.2 -- the exact reader this section exists for -- has to reach :397-399 ('A live pair inside the set PASSes the doctor's beads check ...; a pair outside it -- including the two measured-but-unvalidated rows above -- FAILs as bd-version-vs-schema DRIFT') and reason that their row is not one of 'the two' to learn that their install still passes. Separately, 'the two measured-but-unvalidated rows above' now sits above three rows that each describe some form of measured-but-not-validated; the referent is still recoverable because only two rows carry the literal words 'measured, not validated', but it has to be recovered rather than read.
findings.description: Answer to the brief's question 5. The paragraph itself reads well to someone who has not followed the investigation: it separates what is established from what is not, in that order, and names the task id and date. Two things a cold reader stumbles on. First, the operationally relevant fact for a bd 1.1.2 user -- does my install still pass the doctor? -- moved out of the status column without landing anywhere explicit. Second, the paragraph reports that a lane which installs a pinned, checksum-verified 1.1.2 nevertheless reported 1.3.1 and does not say whether the mechanism is known; a reader can reasonably infer there is an explanation they are missing, when in fact (as of the shipped text) there was not one. Neither makes a claim false, so by the stated stop rule both are v5.0.1, not v5.0.0 -- recorded because question 5 asked.

findings.location: CI run 36971074875 at headSha ed9ea91 -- evidence that post-dates the shipped text; claude-workflow-plugin-wyt3 material
findings.evidence: The new claims in edits A and B about CI are TRUE and I re-derived each from the run at exactly this HEAD rather than from the commit message. (1) 'That lane installs bd 1.1.2 from a pinned, sha256-verified tarball' -- .github/workflows/test.yml:437-441, and in the log '/tmp/beads.tar.gz: OK' then 'bd version 1.1.2 (20e493e56: HEAD@20e493e569c9)' at 05:54:59. (2) 'the doctor running inside it reported installed bd 1.3.1 / store schema v66' -- confirmed verbatim at 06:38:53. (3) 'no second bd is downloaded anywhere in the job' -- confirmed three ways: the job defines exactly one bd download; `type -a bd` in the failure dump shows ONE entry, 'bd is /usr/local/bin/bd'; and filtering the 'Run L1 suite' step for 'releases/download|github.com/steveyegge|curl .*beads' returns nothing while the same filter over the whole log finds the install step's URL 3 times. Neither MCP server can pull one either -- bd-mcp deps are {@modelcontextprotocol/sdk, zod} over 92 lockfile packages, code-graph-mcp adds sql.js and web-tree-sitter over 95, and no lockfile key matches beads|/bd$|bd-. (4) 'The ceiling row is unaffected: l1-doctor-bd-max runs the same checks and passes them on the bd it pins' -- job 110724973639 conclusion=success, 223 assertions, installing 'bd version 1.3.0 (f45...)' and disclosing '[8a] measured: bd-version-vs-schema pin OK: 1.3.0:66 is in the validated set'. That is a direct observation of the ceiling lane measuring its own pin, not the weaker inference from set membership. NEW, and not in any shipped text: the binary at /usr/local/bin/bd printed 1.1.2 at 05:54:59 (install step) and again at 05:55:08 (Verify dependencies), then 1.3.1 at 06:38:53 -- same path, one bd on PATH, no download logged in between. The file at the installed path was replaced during the run.
findings.description: Recorded as evidence, not as a defect: every CI claim the two edits make holds, and the wording stays on the correct side of the C9 line -- 'what is NOT established', 'consistent with never having measured the floor at all' and 'would have observed' are all marked as inference, while '1.1.2:53 is a correct pair' is asserted flatly and is the one that was measured. The in-place replacement above is the answer ed9ea91's disclosure feature was built to surface, now visible in the first run that carries it, and it strengthens rather than undermines the shipped counterfactual: a binary that replaces itself with the newest release would have landed on 1.3.0:66 before 1.3.1 existed, which is exactly what the README and the header say. I did not establish WHAT performed the replacement and make no claim about it; the repo writes to /usr/local/bin only in .claude/tests/linux/Dockerfile, which this job does not run.

findings.description: Housekeeping, surfaced because both items affect whoever approves rather than this diff's correctness. The stale hash is a mechanical refusal waiting to happen, fixed by one `bash .claude/scripts/impact-report.sh claude-workflow-plugin-ishe`. The review artifact sitting in its own change set is the hazard qa.md warns about and is worth knowing before the approval binds. Cheap checks, all green at this tree: workflow-doctor.test.sh 228 assertions rc 0 (matching ed9ea91's stated count); make lint rc 0; `workflow-manifest.sh generate .` diffs IDENTICAL against manifests/v5.0.0.sha256 at 140 rows, and the edited doctor's own sha256 (2082a15c3a34eded...) equals its manifest row exactly. `git status --porcelain` was byte-identical before and after the entire review -- three modified files and the r1 artifact, nothing else; no mirror was built and nothing was symlinked.
